wording: - **In scope.** An individual with a residence or habitual abode in Germany, taxed on worldwide income (§ 1(1) EStG), who earns profit from self-employed work (§ 18 EStG, Anlage S) or a trade (§ 15 EStG, Anlage G), and works out profit by the cash method (§ 4(3) EStG). Single or jointly assessed with a spouse.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Freiberufler or trade.** Only a trade pays trade tax and gets the § 35 credit. The named professions in § 18(1) no. 1 EStG (doctors, lawyers, engineers, architects, tax advisers, journalists, translators and similar) and scientific, artistic, writing and teaching work are Freiberufler. Everything else run for profit is a trade (§ 15(2) EStG). Unclear cases: refer (see de-einkommensteuer-freelancer).
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Cash method or books.** A trader must keep books once the tax office gives notice after turnover over EUR 800,000 or trade profit over EUR 80,000 in a year (§ 141 AO). A Freiberufler can always use the cash method. Books are out of scope here.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Who must file.** Without wages, anyone whose total income is above the basic allowance (twice it for spouses) (§ 56 EStDV). With business income the return and the EÜR must be sent electronically (§ 25(4) EStG, § 60(4) EStDV).
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Out of scope.** Companies (GmbH, UG): de-corporate-tax. Partnerships (GbR, OHG, KG, PartG), whose profit is fixed at partnership level. Non-residents with German business income: de-non-resident-tax. Selling or closing the business, extraordinary income (§ 34 EStG), retained profits (§ 34a EStG), foreign income and treaties.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: **Cars.** A car used more than 50% for business can be a business asset: all costs are expenses and private use is added back at 1% of the gross list price per month (§ 6(1) no. 4 EStG), or by logbook. A private car used for business trips: EUR 0.30 per km or the actual cost share. Trips from home to the own office count only at EUR 0.38 per km one way. Electric and hybrid cars have special rules: refer.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: **Phone and internet.** Deduct the business share shown by records. The employee flat rate from the wage tax guidelines is not a rule for the self-employed.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: **Mixed and unknown items.** Default to no deduction until the client confirms the business share.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: **Step 2: from profit to taxable income** (§ 2 EStG). Profit plus any other income = total income. Less special expenses: pension contributions within the cap; basic health and care cover in full; other insurance only if the cap has room; church tax paid, donations, or the EUR 36 lump sum. Less extraordinary burdens and child allowances (see de-employee-income-tax). Round down to whole euros.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: **Step 3: tax.** Apply the tariff (or splitting). For a trader, subtract the § 35 credit: the lowest of 4.0 × Messbetrag, the tax that falls on trade income (positive trade income / all positive income × tariff tax), and the trade tax actually payable. Unused credit is lost. Then the surcharge on the tax after the credit, and church tax on the tax before the credit (§ 51a(2) EStG). Subtract prepayments paid.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: **Losses.** A loss offsets other income of the same year, then goes back one year or forward without time limit (§ 10d EStG; see de-einkommensteuer-freelancer).
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Late-filing surcharge (§ 152 AO).** May be set for any late return. Must be set if the return is not in within 14 months after year end (for 2026: after 29 February 2028), unless the deadline was extended, the tax is nil, or the tax is not more than prepayments and tax withheld. Amount: 0.25% per started month of the tax less prepayments and tax withheld, at least EUR 25 per started month, at most EUR 25,000, rounded down to euros (§ 152(5) and (10) AO).
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Interest (§ 233a AO).** From 15 months after year end (1 April 2028 for 2026) until the notice: 0.15% per full month, 1.8% a year (§ 238(1a) AO), on the balance rounded down to EUR 50. Refunds earn the same.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Late payment (§ 240 AO).** 1% per started month on the overdue amount rounded down to EUR 50. Applies to late prepayments too.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Wrong returns.** Tax evasion is a crime (§ 370 AO). Reckless understatement is an administrative offence with a fine of up to EUR 50,000 (§ 378 AO). Either case: refer.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Non-residents.** A person without a German home or habitual abode is taxed only on German income, including profit from a German permanent establishment or self-employed work done in Germany (§ 49 EStG). Use de-non-resident-tax.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Foreign clients.** Fees from foreign clients for work done in Germany by a resident are German income in full. VAT on cross-border services: germany-vat-return.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Foreign tax, foreign establishment, moving in or out.** Foreign tax credits are in de-non-resident-tax (§ 34c EStG). A treaty may exempt profit of a foreign establishment, which then raises the rate (§ 32b EStG): refer. Departure with shares: leaving-germany-exit-tax.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **§ 7g abroad.** The investment deduction needs the asset used in a German establishment (§ 7g(1) EStG).

section: Example 1: Freiberufler designer, single, normal VAT scheme
wording: Anna is a self-employed designer in Hamburg, single, no church, normal VAT scheme. 2026 fees net of VAT: EUR 72,000. Ordinary costs (software, studio share, insurance, adviser): EUR 9,000. A client dinner: EUR 400 net. A gift to one client: EUR 80. 140 days worked mainly at home without going to the studio, no separate room. All VAT she collected in 2026 she also paid over in 2026, so VAT nets to nil in the EÜR. A laptop for EUR 1,800 net. Basic health and care cover per the insurer's certificate (already net of the 4% cut): EUR 7,200. Private pension (Rürup) EUR 3,000. Prepayments paid: EUR 10,000. (Invented case.)

wording: Bernd runs an online shop in a town with a trade tax multiplier of 360%. 2026 profit EUR 95,000, his only income; no trade tax add-backs. Single, church member at 9%.
